advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Prefer exact-equality on full SHAs (or require the inspected --revision be a full 40-char SHA) rather than startswith-prefix matching in _revision_matches.
evidence: scripts/gerrit_safe_submit.py:57: def _revision_matches(current: str | None, inspected: str) -> bool:
Submit uses server-reported `current` (line 124), so a prefix collision would submit a different-but-prefix-matching revision without failing
advisory.finding: _revision_matches guards staleness with current.startswith(inspected) on an abbreviated (>=12-char) prefix. A NEWER current revision whose full SHA happens to share the inspected 12-char prefix would pass the guard and be submitted, defeating the 'submit exactly the inspected revision' property. The correctness property claimed is an exact-revision match, but the implementation is a prefix match.
scenarios: A newer patch set is uploaded whose full SHA shares the inspected 12-char prefix (astronomically unlikely for full SHAs, but possible for short user-supplied prefixes near the 12-char floor)

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Move the hashtag POST after the staleness/label gate, or accept and document that stamping happens regardless of submit outcome.
evidence: scripts/gerrit_safe_submit.py:96:     detail = _request(...)  # staleness/label checks happen AFTER the hashtag POST
The revision-match refusal (return 2) and label refusal (return 3) both occur after the hashtag has already been written
advisory.finding: The session hashtag is POSTed unconditionally BEFORE the staleness and label/submittability gates, so a change that turns out to be stale (revision mismatch) or unapprovable still gets stamped with the session hashtag and side-effected.
scenarios: A stale/unsubmittable change is stamped with a session hashtag despite the submit being refused

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test where the submit POST raises HTTPError(code=500), asserting main() re-raises rather than returning 2.
evidence: scripts/gerrit_safe_submit.py:128-135 `except urllib.error.HTTPError as exc: if exc.code == 409: ... return 2 raise`
No test injects an HTTPError with code != 409 on the submit POST; the distinction between 'return 2 on 409' and 'propagate on other codes' is only half-verified.
advisory.finding: The non-409 HTTPError re-raise branch in main() (bare `raise` at line 135) is untested — an unexpected HTTP error (e.g. 500/403) at submit is a distinct behavior (propagate, not return 2) with no coverage.
scenarios: Gerrit returns 403/500 on submit; the helper must propagate rather than masquerade as a stale-submit refusal.

blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test where the submit POST raises urllib.error.HTTPError(code=409) after checks pass, asserting main() returns 2 and prints the stale-submit message.
evidence: scripts/gerrit_safe_submit.py:128-134 `except urllib.error.HTTPError as exc: if exc.code == 409: print("refusing stale submit: Gerrit reports revision is no longer current", ...) return 2`

Named violating input: fake_request configured so the GET returns current_revision matching --revision with all labels approved/submittable, then the POST '/a/changes/2764/revisions/.../submit' raises urllib.error.HTTPError(code=409) — the tests never do this.
test_safe_submit_refuses_stale_revision_before_submit only exercises the PRE-submit _revision_matches check (return 2 at line 103), a different code path from the submit-time 409 handler.
PR description: 'Gerrit returns 409 instead of submitting if another session uploaded a newer revision' — this is the headline behavior and it is unverified end-to-end in the script.
blocking.finding: The submit-time HTTP 409 handling in gerrit_safe_submit.main() — the central compare-and-submit safety contract the change advertises — is untested. No test makes _request raise urllib.error.HTTPError(code=409) on the POST .../submit call after the pre-submit checks pass, so the return-2 branch at lines 128-134 has zero coverage.
scenarios: A race where the revision is still current at GET time but a newer patch set is uploaded before the submit POST lands; Gerrit rejects with 409 and the helper must return 2, not crash.
blocking.suggested_fix: Add a test that monkeypatches _request to return a valid/submittable GET detail and raises urllib.error.HTTPError(url, 409, 'Conflict', hdrs, None) on the submit POST, asserting main(...) == 2.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] URL-encode the `revision` path segment in GerritClient.submit_revision() (e.g. `self._q(revision)`), matching how `change_id` is handled.
evidence: `f"/a/changes/{self._q(change_id)}/revisions/{revision}/submit"` — change_id is quoted, revision is not (src/rebar/review_bot/gerrit_client.py:395)
Contrast add_session_hashtag which only interpolates the quoted change_id (line 379)

Reachability: submit_revision is a public method; the in-repo caller (gerrit_safe_submit.py) passes the server-returned `current` SHA (trusted), so the current call site is not exploitable, but the method itself does not constrain/encode the segment — a defense-in-depth gap for any other caller passing untrusted or malformed revision data.
dropped.finding: GerritClient.submit_revision() interpolates the caller-supplied `revision` into the REST path without URL-encoding it (unlike `change_id`, which is passed through `self._q()`). A revision string containing `/`, `?`, or `#` would alter the request path/query rather than being treated as a single path segment.
scenarios: A future caller passes an abbreviated or externally-derived revision string containing a `/` or `?`, silently changing which endpoint is hit.
dropped.suggested_fix: Interpolate `self._q(revision)` instead of the raw `revision` in the submit path.
